summary: Guidance requested: safe off-ramp and preflight checks for combined batching + prefix-cache + custom quantization profile
description: Issue summary: BrightDocs enabled a tenant-scoped optimization bundle (aggressive async batching, prefix/KV caching enabled, and a custom quantization profile built from our quant-tool). After a gradual rollout to 20% of traffic, they observed intermittent 5xx errors and request-level tail-latency spikes. Customer requests a prescriptive safe-offramp and preflight checklist to minimize customer traffic disruption while reverting the optimization. Impact: ~10% of requests for the tenant returning 502/503 over a 30-minute window; several high-priority workflows affected (document summarization). Environment: Dedicated pool in us-east with reserved GPUs (G4-like). Steps to reproduce: 1) Tenant runs route with optimizer-profile: {async_batching: aggressive, kv_prefetch: enabled, quant_profile: custom-v3} 2) Synthetic load at 50 RPS with session lengths ~800 tokens 3) Observe intermittent 5xx and elevated 95/99 latencies. Expected behavior: Stable latency within SLA and normal error rates. Actual behavior: Elevated tail latency and transient 5xx responses after profile enabled. Customer asks for a rehearsed rollback plan, preflight checks to run before re-enabling, and a safe smoke test plan to verify health post-rollback.
steps_to_reproduce: Enable tenant optimizer profile via console: profile=tenant-brightdocs/custom-v3
Set route concurrency to default (no explicit override) and start traffic ramp to 50 RPS
Run long session synthetic job: 800 token prompt / 3-step followups (to exercise KV cache)
Observe metrics in Console: per-route 5xx, token latency breakdown, and GPU utilization
logs: Customer-provided stacktrace (trimmed): RuntimeError: CUDA kernel launch failed; fallback to safe-mode attempted
comments: 2026-03-12T15:00 - Aisha Gomez (Support): Opened ticket after customer reached out; captured logs and requested permission to run tenant-scoped snapshot and a low-impact rollback rehearsal.
2026-03-12T16:10 - BrightDocs (Customer): Confirms runs started after applying custom-v3 quant profile; wants minimum downtime rollback path that preserves session continuity for active users.

2026-03-13T09:18 - Priya Menon (SRE): Initial hypothesis: custom quant kernel selection may be triggering a rare codepath when combined with async batching and long sessions; KV prefetch misses increase memory churn and GC which then exposes kernel timing races.

2026-03-13T12:42 - Engineering (Optimizer team): Requested queueing metrics and the exact quant-tool command used to create profile; suggested staged demote of async_batching and disable prefetched KV for small percentage of traffic as a safe test.
2026-03-14T08:05 - BrightDocs: Approved support team to run non-disruptive preflight checks and a controlled 5% rollback to validate mitigations.
investigation: Checked serving-runtime logs across nodes: node-3 shows repeated kernel_dispatch warnings coincident with 5xx bursts.
Console traces show a correlation: 99th-token-latency spikes when kv_prefetch_miss_rate > 0.25 under high async_batch windows.

Recreated quant_profile with quant-tool using identical flags: reproduced a kernel selection where int8-optim kernel used for certain attention block shapes on GPU type G4-like. We hypothesize a rare mismatch between kernel precondition checks and async batch merging.
No evidence of GPU OOM; memory headroom remains ~15% during incidents.
suggested_action:
1) PRE-FLIGHT (non-disruptive) - Run these checks on a single node during low traffic:
   - 'redwoodctl optimizer inspect-profile --tenant brightdocs --profile custom-v3' to validate kernel map
   - 'redwoodctl serving-stats tail --tenant brightdocs --last 15m --filter kernel_dispatch_failure' to quantify failure rate
   - Run a dry-run replay: 'redwoodctl replay --tenant brightdocs --route doc-summarize --mode dryrun --qps 5 --session-length 800' and collect per-token latencies

2) STAGED OFF-RAMP (safe, low blast radius) - Execute in sequence with 5% traffic gate and observability checks between steps:
   a) Disable async batching for tenant: 'redwoodctl optimizer set --tenant brightdocs --param async_batching=off --staged 5%'
   b) If errors persist, disable kv_prefetch: 'redwoodctl optimizer set --tenant brightdocs --param kv_prefetch=off --staged 5%'
   c) If still failing, revert quant profile to last-known-stable: 'redwoodctl profile rollback --tenant brightdocs --to stable-2026-02-28 --staged 100%'
   Note: Wait 10 minutes after each stage and validate 5xx, 95/99 latency, and GPU kernel warnings before proceeding.

3) QUICK RECOVERY (if high error rate):\n   - Trigger tenant snapshot restore: 'redwoodctl tenant snapshot restore --tenant brightdocs --snapshot pre-opt-2026-03-12' (this rehydrates optimizer state; low risk to long-lived sessions)\n   - If snapshot restore is not possible, apply immediate circuit-breaker on route: 'redwoodctl route set --route doc-summarize --circuit-breaker on --threshold 5xx:2m:3' to route traffic to fallback model variant.

4) POST-ROLLBACK SMOKE TESTS:
   - Warm-up: send 10 sample requests that exercise KV cache patterns; verify kv_prefetch_miss_rate falls to baseline (<0.05)
   - Run 30-minute stability test at customer-typical QPS and confirm 99th latency <= baseline + 150ms and 5xx rate <0.1%
   - Ask customer to run critical workflows and confirm success for active users

5) LONGER-TERM MITIGATION SUGGESTIONS:\n   - We will create a determinism test in our CI to validate quant kernel selection for merged async batches on G4-like hardware\n   - Consider creating an automated circuit-breaker that disables async_batching + custom quant profile combo if kernel_dispatch_failure is observed > 0.1% over a 10-minute window
resolution: In Progress - awaiting staged 5% off-ramp validation. Support and SRE to run preflight checks on 2026-03-14 16:00 UTC. If 5xx rate and kernel_dispatch_failure drop to baseline within 10 minutes, proceed with staged 100% revert of quant profile; otherwise escalate to Eng for hotfix.
follow_up_actions: SRE to coordinate 5% staged off-ramp and report telemetry snapshot to ticket (Priya)
Optimizer team to reproduce kernel_dispatch_failure in isolated CI matrix and provide hotfix or guardrail within 48 hours
Support to schedule a customer-facing post-mortem call within 24h of incident resolution
